heat_stress.label: Heat stress and urban climate
heat_stress.description: Datasets and indicators related to high temperatures, thermal comfort, and urban heat island effects. Useful for public health planning, energy demand forecasting, and climate adaptation studies.

air_quality.label: Air quality and atmospheric composition
air_quality.description: Atmospheric composition and air quality indicators relevant to public health exposure assessment, regulatory compliance, and environmental monitoring. Covers European high-resolution reanalysis and global composition forecasts from CAMS.

wildfire.label: Wildfire and fire weather
wildfire.description: Fire weather indicators from CEMS EFFIS covering fire danger rating and fire weather conditions. Covers the historical record from 1940 to present at global 0.25° resolution.

ocean_and_water.label: Ocean, water, and cryosphere
ocean_and_water.description: Ocean and inland water products including satellite sea surface temperature, ORAS5 ocean reanalysis, lake water levels from radar altimetry, and satellite soil moisture.

agriculture_and_land.label: Agriculture, vegetation, and land surface
agriculture_and_land.description: Agriculture, vegetation, and land surface datasets covering agrometeorological indicators (AgERA5), satellite vegetation indices (LAI, FAPAR), surface albedo, and land cover classification.

renewable_energy.label: Renewable energy resources
renewable_energy.description: Wind and solar resource datasets for renewable energy siting and planning. Uses ERA5 upper-level wind components (u100/v100) for offshore wind resource assessment.

climate_projections.label: Climate projections and seasonal forecasts
climate_projections.description: Future climate from CORDEX regional downscaled projections and seasonal forecasts for the next 1-4 months. Covers temperature, precipitation, and wind under multiple emissions scenarios.

climate_trend.label: Climate trend and anomaly
climate_trend.description: Long-term climate trend and anomaly analysis using ERA5 reanalysis from 1940 to present. Suitable for climate change communication, risk assessment, and regional planning.

flood_risk.label: Flood, precipitation, and hydrology
flood_risk.description: Precipitation and hydrological products from ERA5 and satellite precipitation datasets relevant to flood hazard and exposure assessment.

radiation_and_clouds.label: Radiation, clouds, and Earth energy budget
radiation_and_clouds.description: Radiation and cloud products from ERA5 surface radiation fields and satellite-derived cloud properties.

urban_heat_island.label: Urban heat island assessment
urban_heat_island.typical_question: How much warmer is the city centre than surrounding areas in summer?
urban_heat_island.notes: ERA5 0.25° resolution captures the broad urban-rural gradient. For finer detail over land combine with reanalysis_era5_land at 0.1°. Subtract the 1991–2020 monthly climatology to produce a temperature anomaly map.

heatwave_frequency.label: Heatwave frequency and intensity
heatwave_frequency.typical_question: How many days exceeded 35°C in this region last summer?
heatwave_frequency.notes: Extract daily maximum temperature and count exceedances above a threshold (35°C = 308.15 K). ERA5 is hourly so daily_max accurately captures peak heat.

utci_exposure.label: UTCI outdoor heat stress exposure
utci_exposure.typical_question: How many days fall in the strong or very strong UTCI heat stress category?
utci_exposure.notes: UTCI thresholds in Kelvin: >319 K extreme stress, 311–319 K very strong, 305–311 K strong. Values stored as Kelvin; subtract 273.15 for Celsius UTCI. Mean Radiant Temperature (mrt) is the companion variable for urban studies.

cooling_degree_days.label: Cooling degree days for energy planning
cooling_degree_days.typical_question: What is the annual cooling degree day total above 18°C?
cooling_degree_days.notes: Cooling degree days (CDD) = sum of (T_daily_mean - 291.15 K) for all days above the threshold. Annual CDD drives energy demand projections.

high_resolution_temperature.label: High-resolution European temperature — CERRA
high_resolution_temperature.typical_question: What is the temperature at 5km resolution over complex terrain?
high_resolution_temperature.notes: CERRA is the European Arctic regional reanalysis at 5.5 km resolution — approximately 5x finer than ERA5. Essential for Alpine, coastal, and Scandinavian regions where ERA5 is too coarse. Covers 1984 to present.

pm25_exposure.label: PM2.5 population exposure mapping
pm25_exposure.typical_question: Which districts experience the highest PM2.5 levels in winter?
pm25_exposure.notes: Units are µg/m³ — GIS-friendly, no conversion required. WHO annual guideline is 5 µg/m³; EU annual limit is 25 µg/m³. CAMS Europe resolution is 0.1° (~11 km), covering 2013–2023.

no2_hotspots.label: NO2 traffic and industrial hotspot mapping
no2_hotspots.typical_question: Where are NO2 concentrations consistently highest?
no2_hotspots.notes: NO2 in µg/m³. EU annual limit is 40 µg/m³. High values indicate road traffic corridors and industrial zones. Seasonal patterns (higher in winter due to lower mixing) reveal emission sources.

ozone_exceedance.label: Ozone exceedance days
ozone_exceedance.typical_question: How many days exceeded the WHO ozone guideline of 100 µg/m³ peak?
ozone_exceedance.notes: Ground-level ozone is highest in summer under strong radiation and photochemical smog conditions. Count days exceeding 120 µg/m³ (EU target) or 100 µg/m³ (WHO guideline).

combined_heat_pollution.label: Combined heat and air pollution exposure
combined_heat_pollution.typical_question: Where do extreme heat and elevated PM2.5 occur together?
combined_heat_pollution.notes: ERA5 is 0.25°, CAMS Europe is 0.1°. Use fuse(resolution='coarser') to resample ERA5 onto the CAMS grid before compound analysis. Pixels with simultaneous t2m > 308 K and pm2p5 > 25 µg/m³ mark the highest compound risk zones.

global_aerosol.label: Global aerosol and atmospheric composition
global_aerosol.typical_question: What are the global aerosol optical depth patterns?
global_aerosol.notes: EAC4 covers 2003–present at 0.75° resolution. AOD > 1.0 indicates dense smoke or dust; > 0.4 indicates moderate aerosol loading. Useful for dust transport, wildfire smoke, and industrial pollution at continental scale.

air_quality_forecast.label: Near-real-time air quality forecast
air_quality_forecast.typical_question: What will PM2.5 and ozone be over the next 4 days?
air_quality_forecast.notes: Forecast data extends up to 4 days ahead. Daily maximum is the operationally relevant statistic for EU Air Quality Directive compliance and public health advisories. The forecast store suffixes every pollutant with _conc (o3_conc, no2_conc, pm10_conc, co_conc, so2_conc).

fire_danger_mapping.label: Fire weather index mapping
fire_danger_mapping.typical_question: Where is fire danger highest this fire season?
fire_danger_mapping.notes: FWI > 50 is classified as extreme fire danger. The historical record from 1940 to present enables multi-decade trend analysis. Combine with satellite_lai_fapar for vegetation-weighted fire risk assessment. Also available: ffmcode, dufmcode, drtcode (fuel moisture), infsinx, fbupinx, fdsrte.

fire_season_trend.label: Fire season danger trend — multi-decade
fire_season_trend.typical_question: Has fire danger increased over the past 30 years in this region?
fire_season_trend.notes: Annual mean FWI reveals long-term trends driven by warming and drying. Mediterranean, Iberia, and California show statistically significant FWI increases in ERA5-based fire weather reanalysis since 1980.

sea_surface_temperature.label: Sea surface temperature mapping
sea_surface_temperature.typical_question: Where is sea surface temperature above historical norms?
sea_surface_temperature.notes: Satellite SST at 0.05° resolution — much finer than ERA5 SST. Covers 1979 to present from multi-sensor fusion. The Mediterranean recorded record SST exceeding 30°C in summer 2023.

ocean_reanalysis.label: Ocean heat content and sea level — ORAS5
ocean_reanalysis.typical_question: How has sea surface height changed over the past decade?
ocean_reanalysis.notes: ORAS5 at 0.25° monthly from 1958 to present. Also available: ocean temperature (sosstsst), salinity (sosaline), sea ice thickness (iicethic). Sea surface height (sossheig) is provided as anomaly relative to model mean.

soil_moisture_drought.label: Soil moisture and agricultural drought monitoring
soil_moisture_drought.typical_question: Which regions are experiencing soil moisture deficits this season?
soil_moisture_drought.notes: Units: m³/m³ volumetric water content. Values range from ~0.05 (very dry) to ~0.5 (saturated). Compare against the 1991–2020 climatological mean to identify drought anomalies. Covers 1978 to present at 0.25°.

lake_water_level.label: Inland lake and reservoir water level monitoring
lake_water_level.typical_question: Is this lake or reservoir at historically low levels?
lake_water_level.notes: Derived from satellite radar altimetry for ~2000 lakes globally, covering 1992 to present. Useful for monitoring hydropower reservoirs, irrigation storage, and climate-driven lake shrinkage (e.g. Aral Sea).

marine_heatwave.label: Marine heatwave detection and tracking
marine_heatwave.typical_question: When and where did a marine heatwave event occur?
marine_heatwave.notes: Marine heatwaves are defined as SST exceeding the 90th percentile of the historical baseline for at least 5 consecutive days. The high resolution (0.05°) allows identifying precise heatwave boundaries.

agrometeorological_indicators.label: Agrometeorological indicators for crop assessment
agrometeorological_indicators.typical_question: What were the temperature and precipitation conditions for crops last growing season?
agrometeorological_indicators.notes: AgERA5 is pre-processed for agricultural model inputs: temperature in °C (already converted), precipitation in mm/day. Resolution 0.1° with topographic correction. Covers 1979 to present daily.

vegetation_state.label: Vegetation state and phenology monitoring
vegetation_state.typical_question: When did the growing season start and how dense is the canopy?
vegetation_state.notes: 10-day composites at 1 km resolution. Each subset is one sensor; the Sentinel-3 record runs 2018 to present, and NOAA/SPOT/PROBA subsets extend the CDR back to 1981. LAI > 4 indicates dense canopy; < 1 indicates sparse or stressed vegetation. Also available: fAPAR.

land_cover_change.label: Land cover classification and change detection
land_cover_change.typical_question: How has land cover changed between 2000 and 2020?
land_cover_change.notes: 300 m annual maps from 1992 to present using UN FAO LCCS classification. change_count variable tracks how many times each pixel changed class. Useful for deforestation, urban expansion, and agricultural conversion.

surface_albedo.label: Surface albedo for energy balance studies
surface_albedo.typical_question: How does surface albedo vary seasonally across this region?
surface_albedo.notes: AL_DH_BB is broadband (BB) directional-hemispherical (black-sky) reflectance at 1 km, 10-day composites. Each subset is one sensor; the Sentinel-3 record runs 2018 to present, and NOAA/SPOT/PROBA subsets extend the CDR back to 1981. Used in surface energy balance models. Snow cover significantly elevates albedo (0.7–0.9 vs 0.1–0.2 for bare soil). AL_BH_BB is the companion bi-hemispherical (white-sky) albedo.

agricultural_drought.label: Agricultural drought — soil and vegetation combined
agricultural_drought.typical_question: Which agricultural zones are under drought stress this season?
agricultural_drought.notes: Combine soil moisture deficit with LAI below-normal to identify areas where both soil and canopy are stressed simultaneously. Strong joint signal indicates severe agricultural drought.

offshore_wind_resource.label: Offshore wind resource — 100m wind speed
offshore_wind_resource.typical_question: What is the mean wind speed at turbine hub height over the North Sea?
offshore_wind_resource.notes: 100m wind corresponds to modern offshore turbine hub height. Extract both u100 and v100 then compute wind speed as sqrt(u100² + v100²). The North Sea typically shows mean hub-height wind speeds of 10–12 m/s.

temperature_projection.label: Future temperature change — CORDEX projections
temperature_projection.typical_question: How much warmer will this region be by 2050 under RCP8.5?
temperature_projection.notes: CORDEX at 0.11°–0.44° resolution, 1950–2100. Subtract the historical baseline (1981–2010 mean) to produce a warming anomaly map. Each subset is one {domain}-{scenario}-{step}-{GCM}-{RCM}-{run} combination (213 in total); the one named here is an EUR-11 RCP8.5 EC-EARTH / KNMI-RACMO22E run. Iterate over subsets and average for a robust ensemble estimate.

precipitation_projection.label: Future precipitation change — CORDEX
precipitation_projection.typical_question: Will this region become wetter or drier by mid-century?
precipitation_projection.notes: Mediterranean regions show robust drying signals under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. Northern Europe shows wetting signals. Express as percentage change from the 1981–2010 baseline for communicability. The subset named here is one EUR-11 RCP8.5 run; swap it for other {GCM}-{RCM} subsets to build an ensemble.

seasonal_temperature_forecast.label: Seasonal temperature outlook — 3 months ahead
seasonal_temperature_forecast.typical_question: Will next summer be warmer than average?
seasonal_temperature_forecast.notes: Seasonal forecasts are probabilistic ensemble products at 1° resolution. Skill is highest in the tropics and for the following month. Express as probability of above-normal temperature rather than a point estimate.

seasonal_precipitation_forecast.label: Seasonal precipitation outlook — 3 months ahead
seasonal_precipitation_forecast.typical_question: Is there elevated risk of drought or flooding next season?
seasonal_precipitation_forecast.notes: tprate is the total precipitation rate (m/s); multiply by the accumulation period for a depth. Precipitation seasonal forecasts have lower skill than temperature forecasts but are informative in ENSO-active years. Useful for early-warning drought and flood preparedness planning.

temperature_trend.label: Long-term temperature trend
temperature_trend.typical_question: How has annual mean temperature changed over the past 30 years?
temperature_trend.notes: ERA5 covers 1940 to present — sufficient for 30-year climatological normals and trend analysis. Fit a linear trend per pixel to produce a warming rate map (K/decade).

precipitation_anomaly.label: Precipitation anomaly — wetter or drier than normal
precipitation_anomaly.typical_question: Which regions have been significantly drier than normal this year?
precipitation_anomaly.notes: Total precipitation is in metres of water equivalent per hour (accumulated). Divide by 1000 for mm. Compare against 1991–2020 monthly climatology to identify drought and flood anomaly regions.

sst_trend.label: Sea surface temperature long-term change
sst_trend.typical_question: How has SST changed in this marine region over the past decade?
sst_trend.notes: Satellite SST at 0.05° from 1979 gives a 45-year record for robust trend analysis. The Mediterranean has warmed at approximately 0.04 K/year — faster than the global ocean average.

wind_trend.label: Wind speed long-term trend
wind_trend.typical_question: Has wind speed changed over this region in recent decades?
wind_trend.notes: Extract both u10 and v10, compute wind speed magnitude, then trend. Global terrestrial wind stilling (reduction in wind speed) has been observed since the 1970s in ERA5 with partial recovery after ~2010.

extreme_precipitation.label: Extreme precipitation event mapping
extreme_precipitation.typical_question: How intense was the rainfall in this flood event?
extreme_precipitation.notes: ERA5 hourly precipitation allows computing daily totals and identifying extreme events. Values in metres — multiply by 1000 for mm. For finer resolution over land, use reanalysis_era5_land (0.1°).

precipitation_trend.label: Long-term precipitation trend
precipitation_trend.typical_question: Are extreme rainfall events becoming more frequent?
precipitation_trend.notes: sat_gauge_precip is the satellite/GPCC gauge-corrected blend at 0.1°, monthly means 1983–2023 (the daily-mean subset serves raw satellite_precip and the shorter 'precip' field). Useful for regions with sparse rain gauge networks (tropics, ocean). Combine with ERA5 for a multi-source assessment.

satellite_precipitation.label: Satellite-derived precipitation — global coverage
satellite_precipitation.typical_question: What was total rainfall in this tropical region last month?
satellite_precipitation.notes: Useful where ERA5 is uncertain due to sparse assimilated observations. Covers global tropics and sub-tropics at 0.1°, monthly 1983–2023. For daily fields use the daily-mean subset (variable precip, 2000–2021).

surface_solar_radiation.label: Surface solar radiation — energy and climate
surface_solar_radiation.typical_question: What is the total solar energy reaching the surface in this region?
surface_solar_radiation.notes: Surface solar radiation downwards (ssrd) in J/m². Divide by 3600 for Wh/m² or by 3,600,000 for kWh/m². Complement with fdir (direct radiation) for concentrated solar power siting.

cloud_properties.label: Cloud properties and cloud fraction
cloud_properties.typical_question: How cloudy is this region and what types of clouds predominate?
cloud_properties.notes: Daytime cloud fractional cover (cfc_day) ranges 0–1; cfc_night is the night-time companion. Also available: cloud top pressure (ctp_day), cloud top temperature (ctt_day), liquid and ice water path (lwp_day, iwp_day). Each subset is one instrument record — the one named here is SLSTR on Sentinel-3A/3B (2018 to present, 0.05°); tcdr-aatsr-envisat and tcdr-atsr2-ers2 extend the record back to 1995.

compatibility_rules.note: ERA5 is 0.25° native, CAMS Europe is 0.1°. Use fuse(resolution='coarser') to resample ERA5 onto the CAMS grid for safe joint analysis.
Both ERA5 and UTCI share the 0.25° grid — no resampling needed before fuse().
ERA5 is 0.25°, satellite SST is 0.05°. Resample SST to 0.25° before joint analysis or use ERA5 SST (sst variable) for a consistent grid.
ERA5 land is 0.1° over land only; ERA5 single levels is 0.25° global. Use ERA5-Land where finer resolution over land is required. Note ERA5-Land does not cover ocean areas.
ERA5 is 0.25° global; CERRA is 5.5 km but covers Europe and the Arctic only. For pan-European analysis use CERRA; for global extent use ERA5.
ERA5 soil moisture is a model variable; satellite soil moisture is observation-based. Both are 0.25° — no resampling needed. Satellite SM covers surface layer only; ERA5 covers multiple soil levels.
CAMS Europe is 0.1°, LAI/FAPAR is 1 km. Resample LAI to 0.1° for joint analysis. Direct pixel fusion without resampling will produce misaligned results.
Satellite SST is 0.05° daily; ORAS5 is 0.25° monthly. For consistent temporal comparison aggregate SST to monthly means before fuse().
Both are 0.1° resolution — compatible for direct joint analysis without resampling. AgERA5 coverage is global; CAMS Europe covers -25° to 45°E.
Fire Weather Index is 0.25°; LAI is 1 km. Resample LAI to 0.25° before combining for vegetation-weighted fire risk analysis.
CORDEX resolution varies by domain (0.11°–0.44°). For anomaly mapping, use ERA5 as the historical baseline and regrid to the same grid as the CORDEX domain being analysed.
